purpose: Pin how a multi-value field becomes bytes so a content-addressed reference does not fork between two honest emitters.

normative_reference.name: RFC 8785
normative_reference.requirement: Array elements are serialized in the order given; canonicalization does not reorder them.

rule: A structured multi-value field is a JSON array with per-field semantics pinned (order-is-semantic or set); it is never string-joined. A field that is a string by contract closes separator collision by validation, a strictly weaker guarantee.

cases.reason: Order is load-bearing, so reordering the array is a different assertion and the digest must fork.
A set is sorted before the object is built, so two input orders recompute to one digest; without the sort they would differ.
Two distinct lists join to the same separator string but canonicalize to distinct array bytes.
A string-by-contract field rejects separator characters inside a value before any canonical bytes are produced.
